item.title: [Due in 4 days] Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education: Microsoft's 30-day reminder names 10 November 2026 as the end of updates
item.description:
The date this page carried for the 23H2 end of updates was read against the November update day; Microsoft has now written 10 November 2026 into the post itself, so the deadline row no longer rests on an inference.

Windows · deadline 2026-11-10 · Count the devices still on Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education and move them to a supported version before the November update; a device left on 23H2 after 10 November stops receiving security fixes.

item.title: [Due in 4 days] Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise and Education reach end of updates in November — 60 days out
item.description:
23H2 is the fallback build most estates parked on while they qualified 24H2 — and 24H2 dies a month earlier.

Windows · deadline 2026-11-10 · Plan one upgrade, not two: any device on 23H2 or 24H2 needs to be on 25H2 or 26H1 before the November update.

item.title: [New] Microsoft asks admins to shorten the time from Windows security update release to deployment, because AI speeds up exploit development from published fixes
item.description:
Patch latency is an exposure window an attacker can now close faster; this post is Microsoft's own argument for a shorter deployment ring on Windows endpoints and servers.

Windows · Measure the median days from Patch Tuesday to 95% deployment per ring, and evaluate Autopatch or hotpatch for the rings that miss it.

item.title: [New] Microsoft publishes guidance for risk-based Windows Server patching: routine, accelerated and emergency paths driven by exploit activity and exposure
item.description:
A defined emergency patch path is what decides how long an exploited Windows Server CVE stays open on domain controllers and internet-facing servers.

Windows Server · Check that an emergency patch path with a tested rollback exists for domain controllers and exposed servers, and that its trigger is exploitation evidence rather than the monthly cycle.
